speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they are triggered specifically by pressure on the earlobe?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Media with Recurrent Perforation and Granulation Tissue.

The patient's history of chronic bilateral ear infections, combined with shooting pain during chewing (temporomandibular joint involvement or referred pain) and specific discomfort from earrings (granulation tissue or skin irritation), suggests that the tympanoplasty may have failed to fully resolve the infection or that a new perforation has occurred. I need to confirm if there is any drainage or if the pain is associated with jaw movement specifically.

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy
